subject: Impact assessment: compressing evaluation window for BrightEdge MAP
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BrightEdge MAP — compression risk summary and ask

Team,

Quick summary: BrightEdge (BD-783) just told us procurement requires a 30-day security/legal review before they can sign the SOW. Their original MAP assumed a 14-day evaluation window and sign-by date of 8/01 — that timeline is now at risk.

Impact:
- Eval window compression (we proposed 2 weeks of hands-on eval) will reduce the time for KPI verification and increase likelihood of a post-sign regression.
- Procurement hold pushes close by ~2–4 weeks unless we change the MAP scope.
- Sales commission/forecast implication: Q3 commit at risk.

Attachments: MAP_v3.xlsx (current mutual action plan), SOW_draft_v2.pdf

Ask:
1) I need proposed mitigation options we can present to BrightEdge today (phased pilot, reduced feature surface, exec POC extension terms, or temporary licensing arrangement).
2) Legal/Contracts: can we agree a conditional billing hold and 'pilot-only' SOW that shortens sign-off friction? Laura, can you weigh in on acceptable stop-gap terms?
3) Rishi/Neha: please quantify technical gating criteria that MUST be validated in a compressed window vs. what can be validated post-sign.

I'll consolidate and propose a new MAP version to send to Tom by EOD.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP_v3.xlsx (xlsx)]
[Attachment: SOW_draft_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@brightedge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@brightedge.com>, Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@brightedge.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T12:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightEdge MAP — compression risk summary and ask

Marissa — thanks for the heads up and for sharing the MAP. A couple points from procurement/security:

- Legal needs the full SOW review cycle (standard for us) — we're unlikely to bend below ~30 days for contract & security sign-off given our internal cadence.
- We are open to continuing the eval in a fenced pilot mode that won't require full company-wide sign-off, but that needs to be explicitly scoped (limited users, data scopes, and a fixed expiration date).
- Can you provide a short delta SOW (pilot SOW) and a stripped MAP that shows phased milestones we can do pre-sign?

Operational ask: provide a proposal that lets us run an official, timeboxed pilot with the features necessary to validate the top 3 KPIs (throughput, latency at 95th percentile, and embedding accuracy on our 50k queries). If we hit those, procurement will prioritize the SOW.

If you can give us a pilot SOW + a short exec note on rollback/fallback controls by EOD tomorrow, we'll fast-track the internal review.

—Tom
Tom Alvarez
Director of Data Platforms, BrightEdge Analytics
[Procurement contact: procure@brightedge.com]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-07-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightEdge MAP — compression risk summary and ask

Marissa — cc'ing product for quick triage. Proposed mitigations we can put in a revised MAP (short bullets for Tom):

Option A — Timeboxed pilot (recommended)
- Scope: 3 core features (query generation, embeddings search, reranking) limited to a 10-user pilot group and 1 dataset (50k queries).
- Validation metrics: 95th latency < 220ms (on their infra profile), embeddings MRR > 0.42 on their holdout.
- Controls: data retention = 7 days, read-only mode for production traffic, auto-disable after 30 days unless SOW signed.
- Rollback: immediate key revocation & managed dataset purge script.

Option B — Reduced eval surface + engineering support
- Scope: full-feature eval but with synthetic traffic generated by Redwood to hit their SLA curves; less reliance on their production dataset.
- Trade-off: quality validation limited; better for throughput/latency validation only.

Option C — Conditional go-live clause in SOW
- Sign SOW with billing hold and 30-day cure window tied to production KPIs; billing starts only on exec sign-off after KPI acceptance. Legal needs to approve language but this reduces procurement friction.

Action items (for MAP v4):
- Marissa: draft pilot SOW (short) and a 1‑page exec summary.
- Laura: confirm whether billing-hold wording acceptable and fastest path to an addendum.
- Neha/Priyom: list the absolute minimum telemetry/events we must capture during pilot to certify success.

I'll prepare a short technical acceptance checklist we can attach to the MAP.

—Rishi
Principal Solution Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@brightedge.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-07-21T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: BrightEdge MAP — compression risk summary and ask

Tom — thanks for the quick clarity. Attached is a concise MAP_v4_proposal.xlsx and a proposed pilot SOW (high-level) that implements Rishi's Option A. Highlights:

- 30-day, timeboxed pilot scoped to 10 named users and the 50k query dataset (pilot dataset will be isolated).
- Billing hold clause: no billing or invoicing during the pilot period; on successful KPI certification the SOW transitions to full commercial terms (DocuSign link included).
- Fail-safe: immediate key revocation and data purge if pilot is terminated for any reason.
- Exec sync: propose a 20-minute call next Tue 7/25 to align stakeholders and confirm KPI owners.

Next steps for you if acceptable:
1) Confirm pilot users and point of contact for security review (procure@brightedge.com is fine).
2) Approve the pilot scope in MAP_v4_proposal.xlsx or request a single change.
3) If green, I'll send the DocuSign pilot SOW with the billing-hold clause and set the exec sync.

If procurement still requires the full security packet before pilot start, we can sandbox the pilot on a Managed Demo environment with synthetic data while security runs in parallel. That will preserve momentum though slightly reduce fidelity.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0198
[Attachment: MAP_v4_proposal.xlsx (xlsx)]
